in_text_mentions: Imaging, particularly high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) of the chest, is a key component of the noninvasive evaluation of suspected PVOD. Although not diagnostic in isolation, HRCT can reveal characteristic radiographic features that raise clinical suspicion. A classic triad—comprising centrilobular ground-glass opacities, smooth interlobular septal thickening, and mediastinal lymphadenopathy—is present in the majority of patients, with most exhibiting at least two of these findings Figure 1 [8,29,30,31].
